title: What is truth? (John 18:28–38)
hookLine: Pilate asks and doesn't wait for an answer
carry: I find in him no fault at all

lines: A BIG QUESTION, AND THE DOOR.
cards: Out, in, out again. In today's scene Pilate can't stay put. The priests who bring Jesus won't go into the governor's hall, John says, so they can keep themselves ready to eat the Passover.
So Pilate goes out to them, back in to the prisoner, then out again. Watch his feet as the morning goes on.
In the middle of all that coming and going, he asks a question as large as any in the Gospel, then heads for the door.

teach.h: MY KINGDOM IS NOT OF THIS WORLD.
teach.b: It's early morning. Jesus is brought to the Roman governor's headquarters. Pilate is the man who will soon say he has power to crucify, and the talk shuttles between him and the prisoner.
Pilate asks: are you a king? Jesus answers, in the King James Bible, "My kingdom is not of this world."

teach.h: BORN TO BEAR WITNESS TO THE TRUTH.
teach.b: Then he says what he came for: "To this end was I born, and for this cause came I into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth. Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice."
Pilate says three words: "What is truth?" And then, John tells us, he went out again. He asks the biggest question in the room and leaves before anyone can answer.
Four hundred years ago the English writer Francis Bacon opened an essay with this scene: "What is truth? said jesting Pilate, and would not stay for an answer." Was he jesting? Nobody knows his tone.
Readers have heard it as sneering, as weary, as a politician who's heard too many sincere men. The Greek word for truth is aletheia, and in John it's more than correct information.
Jesus has already said, I am the way, the truth, and the life.
So in John's telling, Pilate asks what truth is while Truth stands in front of him.

teach.h: ALETHEIA, STANDING IN FRONT OF HIM.

teach.b: Then Pilate goes out and tells them, I find in him no fault at all.

how: Christians read Jesus's trial before Pilate during Holy Week, and churches that say the Apostles' Creed name him in it: suffered under Pontius Pilate.

o: a Roman soldier who guarded the tomb
the high priest who questioned Jesus at night
the Roman governor who asked what truth is

"when he had said this, he went out again."

games.q: you're Pilate. the prisoner says he came to bear witness to the truth. what do you do?
o: ask him to explain, and listen.
ask 'what is truth?' and walk out.
set him free on the spot.
games.why: he asks the biggest question in the room and leaves without waiting for an answer.

practice: Think of a question you ask without waiting for the answer: how are you, said in passing, or one you put to God or to yourself before changing the subject. Ask it again, slowly, and this time don't move on; just wait.
If you pray, ask it in prayer and leave a silence after it.
